claims.explanation: The author correctly identifies genuine unresolved meaning and coverage: C01 names BOTH NPSE-VE and NPSE-VP, eight tasks, and 1k/10k/100k simulations. E01 repeats those budgets; fig2_nonseq_c2st.md, benchmark_nonseq.md and benchmark_nonsequential.md contain only approximate 10k/100k extracts. Comparable has no supplied equivalence margin, and the majority-based falsifier is not the same as requiring both variants to beat NPE everywhere. Alternate extracts disagree materially, for example Lotka Volterra NPSE-VE at 10k is approximately 0.75, 0.68 or 0.80. Reported comparisons can represent directional cells but cannot decide unspecified comparability or recover missing 1k cells. Approximation alone would make an otherwise meaningful declaration inconclusive, not unexpressible; the actual blockers are the full scope and comparability/quantifier ambiguity. Retain the skipped/unclear annotation; no full missed declaration is established.

I inspected fig3_seq_c2st.md and E02: TSNPSE-VE and TSNPSE-VP are separate operands against SNPE-C and TSNPE on SLCP and Lotka Volterra, and E02 also includes 1k results absent from that extraction. The statement permits VE and/or VP; the falsifier likewise refers to BOTH variants, rather than selecting one preferred variant in advance. Reported BestBaselineConsistencyDomain can compare one fixed treatment against both baselines, but it has no existential alternative between two treatments. ClaimSpec combines properties by AND, so two fixed-variant properties strengthen and/or to both, and choosing the observed better variant silently changes the assertion. A task/budget-dependent minimum over variants is also not a schema operation. The no-relation skip is therefore justified for the full assertion; approximate data is not itself the reason to skip.

E03/C03 require TSNPSE dominance over SNPSE-A and SNPSE-B AND SNPSE-C failure at C2ST approximately 1. Both fig6_seq_comparison.md and fig6_sequential_comparison.md tabulate A/B/TSNPSE at 10k and 100k for SLCP and GLU, but explicitly omit C from their numeric tables. Its approximately-one failure remains prose. The two extracts also differ numerically, and TSNPSE is not resolved to a VE/VP variant. A pairwise or best-baseline scan of A and B would be only a partial declaration; aliases cannot manufacture C cells or identify an unspecified SDE. ReportedEvidence reads comparable numeric table cells, not the omitted-method prose, so the whole-claim prose-only skip is correct. No C2ST constant or synthetic measurement is supplied to make it appear complete.

Fig4c_pyloric_valid.md and pyloric_rounds.md report TSNPSE/SNPSE-VP, TSNPE and SNVI at matched 30k through 190k budgets under the nine-round, 30000+20000-per-round setup. The final 81% is not safely discardable as an illustrative score: the falsifier explicitly rejects either baseline at >=81% at any matched budget and also rejects failure to exceed both baselines across all budgets <=200k. Reported pairwise/cohort comparisons can express the latter directional condition but do not provide a fixed 81%-threshold predicate or complete final-value condition. Initial-round ties and approximate values do not license dropping that budget from the claim. The generative invariant/threshold domains consume run batches/null experiments, not this fixed curve; substituting synthetic runs would invent evidence. The full no-relation skip is correct; the differing approximate baseline percentages in the alternate extraction are not averaged or selectively chosen.

C05 compares VE and VP on three low-dimensional and four high-dimensional tasks; E01/E02 cover different nonsequential NPSE and sequential TSNPSE methods. The low-dimensional directional comparison is straightforward in the tables, but high-dimensional comparably or better has no margin/test, and the falsifier instead refers to correlation with parameter dimensionality rather than a specified task-budget conjunction. Fig2_nonseq_c2st.md and fig3_seq_c2st.md report approximate 10k/100k values; alternate nonsequential extracts can disagree about which variant is lower. The reported schema supports fixed directional conjunctions, not unspecified equivalence or correlation with dimensionality. A <= comparison, a fixed variant choice or an assumed pooling across sequential/nonsequential methods would settle ambiguities absent from the source. Retain skipped/unclear; neither a complete missed expression nor one authoritative extract is established.
